reasons: [coverage/major] D1 [criteriaAssessments C2; claims CL4; alternatives 'Brickwork per-seat with Relay'; verdict pre-signing question list] The draft says Brickwork fully meets mandatory requirement 2 (C2 assessment, CL4, alternatives 'the only option that meets all three requirements'). The sources do not support that. requirements.md asks for 'Audit logs of app and data changes, retained 1 year'. The Brickwork excerpt only says 'audit logs (1-year retention)' and does not say what is logged. The Formline Enterprise excerpt is the same. Nothing in the packet shows that either vendor logs data changes, which may mean row-level edits made through apps, as well as app and config changes. On a pass/fail gate this is a real gap. The draft does not mention it in C2's weaknesses, and the six pre-signing questions do not include it.

[coverage/major] D2 [criteriaAssessments C1 assessment ('Brickwork passes'); verdict question (2); CL2] Requirement 3 is about on-prem PostgreSQL specifically. The Brickwork source only says Relay enables 'access to private databases'. It does not name PostgreSQL, the versions supported, or whether the queries the apps need will work through Relay. C1 still says 'Brickwork passes on the documents supplied'. That is stronger than CL2's own 'plausibly satisfies' and stronger than the evidence (E5 limitations). The pre-signing questions about Relay cover ports, encryption, attestations and cost, but not confirmed PostgreSQL support over Relay. Whether the only eligible candidate actually passes the gate rests on this point.

findings: [minor/reviewer] D2 [criteriaAssessments C4 assessment; edgeCasesAndFailureModes; calculations (missing)] The newly added C4 text and verdict question (3) raise whether Brickwork builders also need $15 end-user seats, but the draft never puts a number on it. The cost is easy to work out: 12 x $15 = $180 a month. That cuts the 2-year gap from $650 (K10) to $470 a month, and moves the crossover with Formline Enterprise from about 593 (K9) to about 581 end users ((9500 - 12*65)/15 = 581.3). The draft names this as one cause of the thin-margin risk, so the figure should appear next to K9/K10 instead of being described only as something that 'would narrow its lead'.

[minor/reviewer] D1 [verdict (opening conditions sentence); practicalImplications item 3; furtherResearchThatCouldChangeConclusion item 3] The verdict says Brickwork should be signed 'only after it confirms three things in writing'. Two of those three conditions don't hold up as written. (a) The third, 'that Security approves Relay', is an internal approval and not something Brickwork can confirm in writing. (b) The audit-log condition is a hard gate: Brickwork must confirm its logs 'cover both app changes and data changes'. Yet the same verdict, practicalImplications item 3 and furtherResearch item 3 allow a database-side compensating control if Security accepts it. E16-E18 suggest platform logs are usually event-level only, so the most likely outcome is that Brickwork cannot confirm record-level coverage. Read literally, the hard gate would then block signing even though the draft elsewhere describes an acceptable path. The signing conditions should say: data-change coverage confirmed by Brickwork, OR a compensating control that Security accepts.
